summary: The project consists of an educational game that incorporates trade-offs to engage children in interactive training and organic learning, allowing them to acquire real-world knowledge about resource management and Martian colonies.
details:
Ares Base is an educational 3D game created by AndromedaProject to introduce children to the exciting world of space exploration. In the game, players become astronauts on a five-day mission to Mars, where they must take care of a space base, manage resources, complete daily tasks, and solve unexpected problems.

Every day, players receive instructions from Earth and explore different areas of the base. They must take care of a greenhouse by watering plants and adjusting lighting, visit an observatory to discover real NASA astronomy images, monitor solar panels to keep the base powered, and check the magnetic shield. They may also face unexpected events, such as sandstorms and communication failures, making each day a new challenge. At the end of the mission, players receive a report showing their activities and discoveries.

The main benefit of Ares Base is that it turns learning into an adventure. Instead of simply reading about science, children interact with different systems and learn by doing. They discover why water and energy must be carefully managed, how plants can be grown in space, and why astronauts need to monitor their surroundings. The game also introduces topics such as astronomy, solar radiation, oxygen, and life-support systems.

Our goal is to make science more fun and accessible while encouraging curiosity, creativity, problem-solving, and responsibility. We want players to understand that exploring Mars is not just about traveling to another planet; it is also about working together, taking care of resources, and keeping everyone safe.

Ares Base was developed with the help of artificial intelligence tools. The project started as an application with information and static images created using Lovable. After discussions and new ideas, our team decided to transform it into a more interactive 3D game. We used Lovable, ChatGPT with Codex, and Claude during development, and later ported the project to Unity. We also considered NASA resources, including its APOD API for astronomy images and its Veggie experiments as references for the greenhouse.

What makes Ares Base creative is the way it combines different scientific subjects into one adventure. Players can explore the universe, grow food, manage energy, and protect their base, all while experiencing some of the responsibilities of an astronaut. Real NASA images also help connect the game to actual space exploration.

During development, AndromedaProject considered its young audience and the importance of making the experience easy to understand and enjoyable. We discussed how to introduce scientific concepts gradually, how to make tasks interesting, and how unexpected events could challenge players without making the game frustrating. We also planned visual improvements, including colorful environments, friendly characters, intuitive interfaces, and engaging animations.

Ultimately, Ares Base aims to bring the adventure of space exploration closer to children. By combining science, creativity, and gameplay, we hope to inspire young players to become curious about the universe and discover that even a small astronaut has big responsibilities!
